Quick update from runtime triage: initial signals point at request queueing on their dedicated pool. Observations:
- Per-instance concurrency cap hit on several workers (cap=24) leading to requests being queued in the front-end queue; queue depth spikes line up with P95 increases.
- KV cache miss rate increased during the window (cache warmup churn after a small deployment yesterday) which pushed CPU/GPU utilization unevenly and amplified tail latency.
- No model binary changes reported in the last 24h on our side.

Immediate, low-risk mitigations we can apply now (30–60 min):
1) Increase per-instance concurrency cap from 24 -> 40 for the Fintech Neo dedicated pool (short lived, can revert).
2) Bump request queue timeout and enable aggressive prefix KV warmup for their top 10 routes.
3) Open a canary routing rule to shift 5% of traffic to a low-latency tuning profile.

I’ll attach a sample trace for the 04:12 UTC spike (p95-trace-sample.har). If you approve, we can implement 1+2 immediately and monitor.

—Marcus

Adding SRE details from the node logs and rate-limiter dashboards:
- The rate limiter issued soft backpressure when the queue depth hit ~700 requests across the pool; this increased head-of-line blocking for short requests.
- We saw increased CPU scheduling latency on 3 instances (same AZ) which correlates to noisy neighbors during the 04:00 UTC window.

Short-term recommendation (safe rollback plan):
- Apply Marcus's concurrency cap bump to 40, enable KV warmup for the identified prefixes. Monitor P95 and error rate for 30m.
- If P95 does not improve, enable the canary (5% traffic -> low-latency profile) and keep the concurrency bump for up to 6 hours while we debug further.

Longer-term: we should add a dynamic backpressure controller that reduces head-of-line blocking by prioritizing short prompts and preempting long-running requests. I'll open an internal ticket and include proposed metrics.

Michael/Tori —

Summary (executive): during the 03:50–05:30 UTC window on 2026-06-02 we observed a sustained P95 latency regression driven by queueing/backpressure in your dedicated pool. Root causes: per-instance concurrency cap saturation combined with higher-than-expected KV cache churn after a small deployment.

What we did:
- Increased per-instance concurrency cap to 40 (applied 2026-06-02T10:20:00-07:00) — immediate P95 improvement of ~45% in the canary.
- Enabled aggressive KV warmup for top 10 prefixes and extended queue timeout.
- Deployed a 5% traffic canary to a low-latency tuning profile and validated stability.

Current status: metrics are within SLA targets for the monitored routes. We’ve opened an internal engineering ticket to design a dynamic backpressure controller and prioritized scheduling; expected ETA for an initial mitigation rollout is 3 weeks.
